items.titleZh: 法拉利罕见召开发布会力挺领队瓦塞尔
items.summaryZh: 法拉利周二仓促安排电话发布会，宣布对领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔“完全信任”，以平息关于其职位未来的传闻。此举是针对前红牛老板克里斯蒂安·霍纳的言论所引发的媒体“风暴”。
items.originalTitle: Ferrari backs Vasseur as F1 chief in unusual press call
items.summaryEn: Ferrari hastily arranged a press call on Tuesday to declare its full confidence in team principal Fred Vasseur, aiming to end speculation about his future. The move came in response to a growing media storm triggered by comments from former Red Bull boss Christian Horner.
detailZh: 法拉利宣布对领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔“完全信任”，以平息关于其职位未来的猜测。
这一罕见的表态来自周二仓促安排的电话发布会，这家意大利车队表示，此举是对上周末前红牛老板克里斯蒂安·霍纳的言论所引发的不断升温的媒体“风暴”的回应。
霍纳此前为宣传新书接受《泰晤士报》采访时表示，法拉利是他唯一愿意在不持部分股权的情况下效力的车队。
这些言论足以引发关于霍纳可能接替瓦塞尔的讨论，而瓦塞尔在车队中的职位近几站比赛以来一直受到审视。
虽然这类关于法拉利高层变动的猜测早已不是什么新鲜事，但这一次不同的是，瓦塞尔认为这些猜测已经开始损害车队。
他在阿塞拜疆大奖赛之后表示，这是一个令人“沮丧”的局面，因为他不断被问及自己的未来，而这已经影响了维修区内的情绪。
“我们无法在完全平静的环境中工作，”他 感叹道。
正是这一后果，促使法拉利选择公开表态，宣布对瓦塞尔的全力支持。
法拉利首席传播官玛丽亚·孔蒂（Maria Conti）对部分媒体表示：“法拉利的立场很明确，没有改变，法拉利已经做出了自己的选择。我们对弗雷德·瓦塞尔（Fred Vasseur）以及他的团队充满信心，完全的信心，并且我们会继续如此。”
孔蒂强调，当前正是法拉利需要保持“团结和凝聚”的时刻，这正是车队希望在下一场比赛之前平息这些谣言的原因。
孔蒂说：“我们希望避免在马来西亚的下一个比赛周末，焦点只落在这类流言和猜测上。”
F1车队通常不愿意发布声明或进行详细表态，去否认媒体上出现的各种猜测。
此类举动往往适得其反，因为它们只会进一步助长谣言。
在体育界也很出名的一个现象，尤其是在足球领域，就是每当主教练获得董事会的全力支持时，这往往实际上预示着解雇已经近在眼前。
法拉利解释说，这次之所以决定公开表达对瓦塞尔的支持，是因为这些谣言正在对车队造成影响，而且相关报道似乎愈演愈烈而不是逐渐平息。
孔蒂表示，法拉利早已习惯了多次“舆论风暴”——她提到了今年早些时候法拉利Luce电动汽车发布时所引发的那场争议。
但法拉利感到，在阿塞拜疆大奖赛之后，局面已经逐渐失控。
“事实是，在比赛结束后，从周日到昨天，这种传播的力量一直在不断增强，”她说，“通常情况下它应该是逐渐减弱的。”
“所有人——不仅仅是你们媒体，还有来自世界各地的意大利媒体——他们仍在围绕弗雷德编造各种不同的故事，而这没有任何用处。所以我们才决定这么做。”
孔蒂表示，法拉利否认关于瓦塞尔的猜测，不仅仅是为了回应霍纳采访引发的风波，也针对近几周出现的其他传闻。
“我们不打算助长猜测，也不会对来自公司外部的种种假设发表评论，”她说。
“这不仅与《泰晤士报》上关于霍纳先生的报道有关，总体上还存在其他各种猜测。”
但在被问到霍纳谈及法拉利吸引力那番言论时，孔蒂表示：“法拉利一直吸引着非同寻常的关注，许多专业人士渴望成为其中一员，这是很自然的事。”
“这正反映了法拉利真正代表的实力。”
在近期的历史中，通常由法拉利主席约翰·埃尔坎或首席执行官贝内代托·维尼亚发表支持声明，以平息此类猜测。
孔蒂明确表示，现阶段他们无需发表任何声明，因为她的声明已与两人完全保持一致。
“法拉利的立场是明确的，不会改变，”她说。“我身边没有约翰和贝内代托，但我当然与管理层高层保持一致，法拉利已经做出了自己的选择。”
“我们对弗雷德·瓦塞尔和他的团队充满信心。什么都没有改变，我们将继续如此。就是这样。”
当被问到为什么埃尔坎和维尼亚这次没有亲自发表任何言论时，孔蒂回答说：“我们没有预料到要做什么电话会议之类的，因为通常我们在法拉利周围有很多不同领域的沟通，而且不仅仅是车队方面。
“所以为什么仅仅因为一条新闻，我们就需要让董事长和首席执行官站到镜头前？我觉得有玛丽亚出面就足够了。”
detailEn: Ferrari has moved to silence speculation about Fred Vasseur’s future as team principal after declaring its “full confidence” in him.

The unusual move to assert its stance came in a hastily arranged press call on Tuesday, as the Italian team reacted to what it said was a growing media "storm" triggered by comments from former Red Bull boss Christian Horner that were published last weekend.
Horner had told The Times, as part of a piece to publicise his new book, that Ferrari was the only team he would be willing to work at without having part-ownership.
Those comments were enough to fuel talk about Horner being a potential candidate to replace Vasseur, whose role at the squad has been under scrutiny for several races now.
While such speculation about change at the top is nothing new at Ferrari, what is different this time is that Vasseur thinks it has started damaging the team.
He said after the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that it was a “frustrating” situation where he was constantly being asked about his future and that was impacting the mood in the garage.
“We are not working in the perfect serenity," he lamented.
It was this consequence that Ferrari said was the reason why it has chosen to go public and declare its full support for Vasseur.

Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communications officer, told selected media: “Ferrari's position is clear, has not changed, and Ferrari has made its choices already. We have confidence, full confidence, in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.”
Conti emphasised that this was a time when Ferrari needed to remain “united and cohesive”, which is why it wanted to kill the rumours off before the next race.
“We would like to avoid that the next weekend in Malaysia will be focused only on this kind of gossip and speculation,” Conti said.
F1 teams are normally reluctant to issue statements or speak at length to deny speculation that has appeared in the media.
Such moves are often counterproductive as they only serve to further fuel rumours.
It is also well known in sport, too, especially football, that any time a manager has the full backing of the board it can often actually signal a sacking is close at hand.

Ferrari explained that it had decided to go public with its support of Vasseur on this occasion because of the impact that the rumours were having on the team, plus the fact that the story seemed to be getting bigger rather than fading away.
Conti said that Ferrari was used to many “storms of communication” – as she referenced the controversy that had come from the launch earlier this year of the Ferrari Luce electric car.
But Ferrari felt that things had been getting out of control after the Azerbaijan GP.
“The fact is that after the race and on Sunday and yesterday, this power of communication was increasing,” she said. “Normally it is going down.

“Everybody - not just you guys, but also Italian media from all over the world - they are still creating a lot of different stories around Fred, and this is not useful. So this is why we decided to do that.”
Conti said that Ferrari’s move to deny speculation about Vasseur was not just about the fallout from Horner’s interview, but other stories that had emerged over recent weeks too.
“We do not intend to fuel speculation or comment on assumptions coming from outside the company,” she said.
“It is not just related to the story in The Times of Mr. Horner, but in general there was other speculation also.”

But in a reference to the remarks where Horner spoke of the attraction of Ferrari, Conti said: “Ferrari has always attracted extraordinary interest, and it is only natural that many professionals aspire to be part of it.
"It is a reflection of the strength of what Ferrari really represents.”
In recent history, it has been normal for Ferrari chairman John Elkann or CEO Benedetto Vigna to issue statements of support to quell such speculation.
Conti made clear that anything from them was unnecessary at this stage because her statement was made in full alignment with them.
“Ferrari's position is clear and does not change,” she said. “I don't have John and Benedetto with me, but I'm, of course, aligned with the top management, and Ferrari has made its choices.
“There is confidence in Fred Vasseur and his team. Nothing has changed, and we continue to do so. That's it.”

Asked why Elkann and Vigna had not said anything themselves on this occasion, Conti replied: “We were not expecting to do any call and so on because normally we are used to have a lot of communication around Ferrari, in many different areas, and not just Scuderia.
“So why, from any news, do we need to put the chairman and the CEO in front of the camera? I think it's enough, [to have] Maria.”

瓦塞尔的职位近几站比赛以来一直受到审视，他认为传闻已开始损害车队，并在阿塞拜疆大奖赛后称这种局面令人沮丧。
法拉利首席传播官玛丽亚·孔蒂向部分媒体表示：“法拉利的立场很明确，从未改变，法拉利已经做出了选择。我们对弗雷德·瓦塞尔和他的团队抱有完全的信心。”

items.originalTitle: What's next for Williams after Baku B-spec yields mixed fortunes
items.summaryEn: Williams' Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend was a mixed bag: the team reached Q3 for the first time in 2026 but could not start there due to a grid penalty for Carlos Sainz, and while it scored its first points since Monaco with some fortune, Alex Albon crashed out.
detailZh: 巴库站B-spec成败参半，威廉姆斯下一步何去何从
威廉姆斯备受期待的B-spec赛车在阿塞拜疆大奖赛是虚有其表，还是通过了车队的考验、成为迈向2027年更大进步的跳板？
安东内利（梅赛德斯）、塞恩斯（威廉姆斯）
如果要给"成败参半"下一个定义，那正是巴库周末之于威廉姆斯的写照。车队2026年首次晋级Q3，但由于塞恩斯的正赛罚退而未能以此位置起步。车队凭借一些运气拿下摩纳哥站以来的首个积分，但也目睹阿尔本撞车退赛。
阿塞拜疆是威廉姆斯日历上被红圈标出的关键周末，因为车队终于为FW48带来了升级，而这辆赛车已经数月缺乏有分量的改进了。格罗夫车队拿出了全新的底盘，终于达到了规定重量，还带来了新的底板和其他空气动力学部件。
这辆赛车在第二次自由练习中的长距离节奏看起来令人鼓舞，打开了一扇尘封已久的大门，让它回到了包括哈斯、小红牛和奥迪在内的中游集团的水平。
在排位赛中，塞恩斯拿下第九，但因发车罚退滑落到第14位，排在阿尔本身后。从车阵尾部来看，期待已久的得分机会似乎就要落空，直到弗兰科·科拉平托在重启时撞掉了皮埃尔·加斯利和兰多·诺里斯。
“带来这个周末的升级是一次巨大的努力，能带着一个积分离开让人欣慰，”车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯说。“可以看到，我们在第一段长距离中没有节奏，我们需要深挖并弄清楚原因，因为那是比赛中我们无法取得推进的关键环节。”
获得第十名的一分是对工厂里所有辛勤工作的回报，但威廉姆斯的B版赛车真的达到了预期吗？“我认为这正是我们预期的提升幅度，”阿尔本坚持说。“说句公道话，也许我们没预料到能进第三节排位赛（Q3）。但没错，它让我们回到了中游集团的争夺中。”
塞恩斯补充道：“我们的初步感觉是赛车确实快了一点。但我们之前落后太多，即使带来了这么大的升级包，仍然感觉像是在拼命追赶。所以正如所说，在速度方面没有大的惊人惊喜，是一次稳健的进步。”
还有一个附加因素：巴库是真正适合威廉姆斯的赛道，而马来西亚的雪邦和新加坡街道赛却不能这么说——这两条赛道对下压力的要求要高得多。所以，带着一个积分和一次退赛离开，感觉至少错过了机会的一半，如果这意味着威廉姆斯在这三连赛的剩余部分会再次退步的话。
“这条赛道，即使没有升级，也会有利于我们，”阿尔本说。“马来西亚会很有参考价值，能看出我们在一条更注重下压力的赛道上处于什么位置。我们现在也有几天时间来真正理解这套升级包。”
"如果你从大局来看，我们会通过优化让赛车变得更快。但相对于其他车队我们会更慢，因为那条赛道不适合我们。预计我们在马来西亚会退步，然后在新加坡也许能处于中间位置。"
至于阿尔本在第31圈引发安全车的撞车事故，他承认是自己刹车过晚冲过了弯，但也认为这进一步暴露了威廉姆斯的一个关键弱点，而且这个弱点在新旧规则下都一直存在。
"这很奇怪，"他解释道，"我刹车稍微晚了一点，但没晚多少。然后突然来了一阵大风。我以为我会跑宽一点，但从没想到会撞上护墙。"
"我确信在这种情况下我必须主动认错，但与此同时我们之前也遇到过这些问题。我们知道我们的赛车容易抬起前轮，出现三轮着地的情况。我们知道当刹车稍微晚一点时，就可能暴露出这种三轮着地的风险。而有时候一旦发生，前轮抱死对我们赛车造成的代价是巨大的。这种事就是会发生。"
“可以肯定的是，阵风加上同时刹车过晚，赛车就刚好被推过了临界点。超出并不多，只差几米，但这已经太多了。”
或许更合理的看法是，把重新设计底盘同时提升空气动力学性能的过程，当作对车队的一次压力测试。这也是沃尔斯收集证据的一次机会，证明这支位于格罗夫的车队如今比12个月前更有能力推出新部件，同时也是一种纠偏方式，为逐渐展开的2027年赛车项目铺路。
由于新底盘预计会沿用至2027赛季，这意味着一项大工程已经提前完成了。
“我有信心，你们会看到我们现在向前迈进一步，因为那次重大的规则改动已经过去了，”沃尔斯接受天空体育采访时说，“明年还会有一次空气动力学改动和一次动力单元改动。但改动幅度较小，所以我们能够消化。”
“但要追上这个冬天发生的种种混乱，还需要一点时间。我从中得到的真正教训是，我们需要更多的投资，才能仅仅具备跟上前面车队的实力。而成本上限限制了我们的这种投入。”
“（这次升级）方向上是对的。我认为更重要的是，它是我们为明年打下的基础。我们承认今年的进度已经有些落后了，很遗憾，但在迈向2027年之前还有很多工作要做。”
detailEn: What's next for Williams after Baku B-spec yields mixed fortunes
Did Williams' much-vaunted B-spec at the Azerbaijan GP flatter to deceive or has it passed the team's test as a stepping stone to bigger 2027 progress?
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Carlos Sainz, Williams

If there is a definition of a mixed bag, that's what the Baku weekend was to Williams. It progressed to Q3 for the first time in 2026, but didn't start there due to a grid penalty for Carlos Sainz. It scored points for the first time since Monaco, with some fortune, but also saw Alex Albon crash out.

Azerbaijan was a key weekend circled in red on Williams' calendar as it finally upgraded an FW48 starved of significant improvements for months. The Grove team wheeled out an all-new chassis, which was finally on the required weight, as well as a new floor and other aerodynamic parts.
The car's long run pace in FP2 looked encouraging, unlocking a long-shut door to the midfield ballpark that includes the likes of Haas, Racing Bulls and Audi.

In qualifying, Sainz claimed ninth but a grid penalty dumped him back to 14th behind Albon. From the belly of the pack it was looking like a long-awaited chance to score points went begging until Franco Colapinto took out Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris at a restart.

"It's been a mammoth effort to bring the update that we have here this weekend and it's nice to walk away with a point," said team principal James Vowles. "You can see we didn't have the pace on that first stint, and we need to dig and understand that because that was a critical part of the race where we weren't able to make progress."

The point for 10th was a reward for all the hard work in the factory, but did the Williams B-spec really deliver as much as hoped? "I think it's exactly the step we expected," Albon insisted. "Maybe we didn't expect Q3, to be fair to you. But yes, it put us in a midfield fight."

Sainz added: "Our initial feel is that the car feels just a bit quicker. But we were so far away that even though we've been bringing such a big upgrade, it still feels like we are playing a lot of catch-up. So as promised, no big massive surprises in terms of pace, a healthy step forward."

An additional factor is that Baku was a real Williams track, which can't be said from Malaysia's Sepang and the Singapore street circuit which will put a much bigger emphasis on downforce. So, coming away with a point and a DNF feels like at least half of a missed opportunity if it means Williams will regress again over the remainder of the triple header.

"This track, even without the upgrade, it would have favoured us," Albon said. "Malaysia will be telling to see where we are on a much more downforce-focused circuit. We've also got now a few days to actually understand the package.

"If you look at the big picture, we'll make the car go faster in terms of optimising it. But we'll be slower relative to the rest of the field, because that track will not suit us. Expect us to fall back in Malaysia, and then maybe in Singapore we can come somewhere in between."

As far as Albon's crash is concerned, which brought out the safety car on lap 31, he took responsibility for outbraking himself but felt it also further exposed of a key Williams weakness which has carried over across regulations.
"It was odd," he explained. "I braked a little bit later, but not much later. Then we had a big wind gust. I thought I would run a little bit wide, but I never thought I would hit the wall.

"I'm sure I have to hold my hand up in that situation, but at the same time we've had these issues before. We know our car likes to lift the front wheel and we three-wheel. We know when we brake a little bit late, we can expose ourselves to that three-wheeling. And sometimes when it does that, the penalty for front locking is huge on our car. It happens.
"For sure, with the wind gust and braking late at the same time, it just tips it over the edge. It wasn't a huge amount; it was a few metres, but that's too much."

Perhaps it is more constructive to view the process of redesigning its chassis while adding aero performance as a stress test for the team. And a round of evidence gathering for Vowles that the Grove-based squad is now more capable of bringing through new parts than it was 12 months ago, and a way to course correct as the 2027 car project gathers steam.
With the latest chassis expected carry over into the 2027 campaign, that's already one big-ticket item out of the way.

"I'm confident you're going to see us stepping forward now that that big rule change is behind us," Vowles told Sky. "There's an aero change for next year, there's a power unit change for next year. But it's smaller in size so we can absorb it.

"But it's going to take a little bit of time to catch up on the mess that's happened this winter. My real learning from it is we need a lot more investment to bring us just the ability to keep up with those in front. And the cost cap restrains us from doing that.

"[The upgrade] is directionally right. I think more importantly, it's the foundation we wanted to set ourselves for next year. We recognise this year's a little bit behind us, unfortunately, but there's a lot to do in going into 2027."

items.originalTitle: Esteban Ocon: “I’m one of the best, and I’m not afraid to say it”
items.summaryEn: Haas driver Esteban Ocon claimed eighth place at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, his best result of the 2026 season, and reiterated his belief that he is one of the best drivers in the sport.
detailZh: 埃斯特班·奥康：“我是最出色的车手之一，我不怕说出来。”
在巴库取得2026赛季最佳战绩后，奥康欣喜若狂，并希望提醒媒体他在赛车运动中的纪录。
这位哈斯F1车手一直公开表达对自己能力的信心，如今他认为阿塞拜疆大奖赛的成绩证明了自己的实力。
巴库第八名是奥康2026赛季的最高完赛名次。本赛季中，这位法国车手经常因哈斯赛车零部件表现不一致而受限——据了解，这一问题对他的影响大于队友奥利弗·比尔曼，不过情况近来已有所改善。
奥孔现在已经意识到，他在2027年很可能会失去自己的席位，而在巴库的排位赛中他被黄旗阻碍，这让他非常沮丧，因此正赛结束后他才会那么欣喜若狂。
“对这个结果非常开心，”他在以仅仅0.03秒之差被阿尔维德·林德布拉德压过、屈居第七名后说道。“当赛车状态良好时，这就是我们应得的。”
“从本周末一开始我们的赛车就很有竞争力，在进站和安全车的问题上我们都做出了完全正确的决定。我在赞德沃特也做过同样的超车，就在冲线之前完成，所以那也非常棒。而且同样的，在2号弯我又一次抢回了两个位置。”
“所以，是的，这是一场非常非常好的比赛，我对结果真的很满意。我认为这给了所有人良好、积极的氛围，让大家在接下来的三连赛中继续向前迈进。”
“我们即将来到一条非常艰难的赛道，有很多高速弯角，”他在谈到即将到来的雪邦赛道时说道。“而且我们已经展示出我们有一辆相当有竞争力的赛车。对我们来说应该会是两场激动人心的比赛，我很期待。”
当Motorsport.com问到，这是否像是在他经历艰难时期后的一种救赎时，奥康回答：“我可以说这是我应得的——但其余那些糟心事就不配了。”
他还补充道，有趣的是，这也几乎是他在电视采访区对转播商一字不差说过的话：“我和这里的每一位车手都交过手，你知道吗？而且我一直都不逊色于他们。
“我参加过的每一个锦标赛都拿了冠军。我在雷诺方程式赢过比赛，我在卡丁车赢过锦标赛，我赢过（欧洲）F3，我赢过GP3，我在德国房车大师赛半个赛季里跑进了前十，我在F1也赢过比赛。我能做到，你知道吗？”
“我是当今最出色的车手之一，我不怕说出来。”
除了他那句“我赢过每一个冠军”的说法——他很快对此做了补充修正——奥康的说法基本属实。唯一不太准确的地方可能是他2016年参加德国房车大师赛（DTM）的半个赛季，那10场比赛中他只有一次进入前10名，他在这些位置上度过的比赛圈数占其全部比赛圈数的18%。
detailEn: Esteban Ocon: “I’m one of the best, and I’m not afraid to say it”
After taking his best result of the 2026 season in Baku, Ocon was jubilant – and keen to remind the media of his record in motorsport
Haas Formula 1 driver Esteban Ocon has always vocally expressed belief in his ability, and he now feels vindicated by his Azerbaijan Grand Prix result.

Eighth position in Baku marked Ocon’s highest finish of 2026 in a campaign where the Frenchman was often held back by inconsistency in the way Haas’ car parts perform – an issue that is understood to have plagued him more than team-mate Oliver Bearman, although the situation has improved of late.
Ocon is now aware that he’s most likely losing his seat in 2027 and was highly frustrated to have been hindered by a yellow flag in qualifying in Baku, hence his ecstatic reaction after the race.
“Super happy with the result,” he said after being pipped to seventh place by Arvid Lindblad by a mere 0.03s. “When the car is working, that's what we deserve.

“We had a strong car since the beginning of the weekend, we took all the right decisions on the pitstop and on the safety car. I did the same overtake I did in Zandvoort, just before the line, so that was really good as well. And again, two places there as well into Turn 2.
“So, yeah, it's been a really, really good race, I'm really happy with the result. I think it gives just good, positive vibes for everyone to move forward on that triple [-header].

“We are going into a very difficult track with a lot of high-speed corners,” he said of the upcoming Sepang circuit. “And we show that we have a car that's pretty competitive. It should be like two exciting races for us, I'm looking forward to them.”
Asked by Motorsport.com if this felt like redemption in the difficult time he was going through, Ocon replied: “I can say I deserve that – not all the rest of the shit.”
He added, and interestingly that’s something he also told broadcasters nearly word for word in the TV pen: “I've raced with everyone out there, you know? And I've always been on par.

“I won every championship that I've raced [in]. I won races in Formula Renault, I won championships in go-karts, I won [European] Formula 3, I won GP3, I was racing in the top 10 in DTM for half a season, I won in Formula 1. I can do it, you know?
“I'm one of the best out there, and I'm not afraid to say it.”

Other than his “I won every championship” claim, which he swiftly nuanced, Ocon’s statement is mostly true. The only inaccuracy might be his half-season in DTM back in 2016, as he finished in the top 10 just once in 10 races, having spent 18% of all his racing laps in those positions.

items.summaryEn: Williams's long-awaited Azerbaijan Grand Prix upgrade delivered almost its best qualifying performance of the 2026 season, with Carlos Sainz ninth-fastest before his grid penalty, ending a points drought of nearly three months. Gary Anderson assesses the true size of the upgrade by converting laptimes into percentages of the fastest lap each weekend.
detailZh: 威廉姆斯期待已久的阿塞拜疆大奖赛升级带来了几乎是其2026年一级方程式赛季最好的排位赛表现——塞恩斯排位赛成绩第九快（随后接受发车位处罚）——并结束了近三个月的得分荒。
但这次升级的幅度到底有多大？巴库给我们的图景又有多准确？
评估研发究竟是让车队前进、原地踏步，还是实际上倒退，向来都很困难。
我们所能做的，是逐一分析每场比赛的表现，把圈速换算成当周末最快圈速的百分比，这样得出的数字不受赛道长度影响，也不受干湿、湿滑、抓地力高低、冷热甚至风力等条件的影响。
因此，观察四强之外各车队的位置，我们可以利用巴库站以及此前各站比赛的表现来进行比较。
这一比较基于本赛季至今的平均表现，而不是单场比赛。不过，最好和最差的数据，以及出现在哪条赛道，也一并列出供对比。这就是老话所说的：“一燕不成夏”。
威廉姆斯车队抵达巴库时大幅减重。我在空气动力学方面没有看到太多能提升其性能的改动，因此按照以往每增加10公斤重量会损失0.3秒以上单圈时间的平均值来推算，这就是他们减重幅度所对应的水平。
这些百分比是与每个分站周末的最快成绩相比得出的，但我没有将它们重新归零，而是保持原样，因为这样能显示出四强与接下来五支车队之间的差距。
如果只看威廉姆斯在巴库的表现与车队赛季平均水平相比，速度快了0.759%。考虑到这一点，以及威廉姆斯在空气动力学方面并没有多少可圈可点之处，我会把这一进步归因于减重20公斤。
这是一大步，但现实是威廉姆斯本来就不应该以超重状态开始这个赛季。
唯一的瑕疵是，威廉姆斯在五月的迈阿密其实离车群前方以及中游集团更近那么一点点。
不过，在巴库总体排名第六快的车队，比本赛季至今总体第九快要好得多。
这个对比中另一个有趣的事实，我认为它证明了动力单元比底盘更重要：被比较的五支车队中有四支的最佳表现都出现在蒙扎，而我们都知道这是一条非常依赖动力的赛道。
看看阿尔派，它是八月休赛期后第一支在赞德沃特引入重大升级的车队，因此它有更多时间去掌握所需的调校，从而最大化赛车在那里的表现。
最近几场比赛中，它一直在相当显著地缩小与小红牛的差距。
另一个令人担忧的事实是，奥迪尽管做了这么多研发，在巴库却出现了退步。这一点应该让它感到担心。
不过，与阿尔派不同的是，这是奥迪第一次使用这套新空气动力学套件参赛，所以尽管车队内部认为它运作良好，但也许车队没能在仅仅一个比赛周末里把它的潜力完全发挥出来。
是的，这些推测都是基于单场比赛与赛季平均水平对比得出的，但“风之城”巴库与蒙扎很相似：都非常依赖动力单元，而且由于排位赛中的大风条件，整车全部表面上的空气动力学稳健性对圈速至关重要。
对于威廉姆斯来说，这至少是一个意味着它能重新争夺积分的进步，尽管这场比赛并不顺利：亚历克斯·阿尔本撞车退赛，塞恩斯则不得不从最低第18位一路追赶回来。而且正如阿尔本所提醒的，“即使没有这次升级，这种类型的赛道本来也会对我们有利”。
这意味着，只有等我们看过升级后的威廉姆斯FW48在更多类型赛道上的表现之后，才能知道它是否能成为排位赛第三节（Q3）的常客级威胁。
detailEn: Williams’s long-awaited Azerbaijan Grand Prix upgrade produced almost its best qualifying performance of the 2026 Formula 1 season - with Carlos Sainz ninth-fastest before his grid penalty - and ended a points drought of almost three months.
But how big is the upgrade really, and how accurate a picture does Baku really give us?
It’s always difficult to assess if developments have moved a team forward, stood still or, in effect, gone backwards.

All we can do is look at each individual performance and, by converting the laptime into a percentage of the fastest for that given weekend, it gives us a number that is not dependent on the track length, or whether it's wet, dry, slippery, grippy, hot, cold or even windy.
So, looking at the position of the teams outside of the big four, we can build a comparison using performance in Baku and in the previous races.

It is based on the average performance over the season so far, so not individual races. However, the best and worst numbers, and at which circuit, are there for comparison. It’s the old saying: ‘one swallow doesn’t make a summer’.

Williams arrived in Baku with a major reduction in weight. I didn’t see very much aerodynamically that would have improved its performance, so taking the old 0.3+ seconds average loss in laptime for 10 kilos of extra weight, this is what we get as to the level of their weight reduction.

These percentages are compared to the fastest for each individual weekend but, as opposed to re-zeroing them, I am leaving them as they are, as this shows the gaps that separate the big four from the next five teams.

If we just take the Williams performance in Baku compared to the team's season average, it is 0.759% faster. Considering that, and the fact that Williams didn’t have much to talk about aero-wise, I would put that improvement down to 20kg of weight saving.
That’s a big step, but the reality is Williams shouldn’t have started the season overweight.
The only fly in the ointment is that Williams was actually just that little bit closer to the front of the pack, and with that the midfield bunch, in Miami back in May.
However, sixth-fastest team overall in Baku is a lot better than ninth fastest overall for the season so far.

The other interesting fact from this comparison, which I think proves that the power unit is more important than the chassis, is that four of those five teams compared had their best performance at Monza, a circuit we know is very power-dependent.

Looking at Alpine, it was the first to introduce a major upgrade after the August break at Zandvoort, so it has had more time to get on top of the required set-up to maximise its performance around it.
In the last few races, it has been closing the gap down to Racing Bulls fairly dramatically.
Another troubling fact is that Audi, with all its developments, went backwards in Baku. That’s something that should be worrying for it.

However, unlike Alpine it is Audi's first race with this new aerodynamic package, so perhaps the team wasn't able to get the best out of it in one weekend despite the belief within the team being that it was working well.

Yes, these assumptions are all based on just one race compared to the season average, but Baku — the windy city — is similar to Monza: PU-dependent, but because of those windy conditions in qualifying aerodynamic robustness over the complete car’s surfaces is critical to laptime.

For Williams, this is a step that at least means it can challenge for points again even though the race wasn't straightforward, with Alex Albon crashing out and Sainz having to fight his way back from as low as 18th place. And as Albon warned, "even without the upgrade this type of circuit would have favoured us".
This means it won't be until we’ve seen the improved Williams FW48 over a wider range of tracks that we will know if it can be a regular Q3 threat.

Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli says that the Azerbaijan GP was 'one of those days you have to be happy with P5' but adds that he will be 'back at my level' at the Malaysian Grand Prix.

World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan.

Antonelli had finished ahead of Russell in five successive Grands Prix but could only manage fifth in Baku, as the Brit produced his best weekend of the season to claim victory from pole position. The result cut Antonelli's lead over his Mercedes team-mate to 66 points with eight rounds remaining.

Although he salvaged some points, Antonelli's performance left plenty of room for improvement ahead of the second leg of the triple-header, with Malaysia set to host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Asked whether Russell is now his only title rival after Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton dropped more than 100 points back, Antonelli said: "He's always been my rival.

"But I'll make sure next week I re-establish the order and just make sure that I will be at back at my usual level because this weekend I was driving more like my grandma, so it wasn't the usual Kimi.
Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
"Luckily we have another race coming up, and I'm really looking forward to it."

The 20-year-old Italian endured a scrappy weekend, missing a major chunk of track time in practice because of a technical issue before crashing in the first part of qualifying to leave himself starting from 16th on the grid.
"FP1 I did three laps and then missed the half of FP2," Antonelli added. "In FP3, I was getting to the rhythm.
"And then in qualifying, that Q1 one lap was actually okay. But I did a mistake, and then again you re-enter in the bad loop.
Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP.
"Then in the race, I didn't have the confidence, and I just at drove 80 per cent the whole time.
"Realistically, I wasn't there mentally to be able to push 100 per cent as well because I just didn't have the confidence that I had previous weekends, but it will be much better in Sepang."
'Exciting to see battle resume in Malaysia'

Russell underlined his pre-season status as the clear title favourite by winning the season opener in Australia, only to be stunned as Antonelli then claimed the first five victories of his career in successive races.
The Italian remains in control of the title race and has also appeared to hold a race-pace advantage over Russell at almost every circuit.
The Azerbaijan GP saw a dramatic ending as Valtteri Bottas crashed on the final lap as George Russell just beat Max Verstappen to victory by one tenth of a second.
That finally changed in Baku, where Russell backed up a solid run of form by being faster than Antonelli at every stage of the weekend.
Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord insists the strength of Russell's performance won't amount to a psychological blow for Antonelli.
"I don't really think it makes a difference," said Lord, who address the media in Baku in the absence of team boss Toto Wolff.
"I think the drivers, they're setting themselves their own high standards, and they want to perform to those.

"One of the great assets and the great strengths of this team is we've got two drivers who are capable of fighting at the very front, putting the car on pole, delivering flawless race wins, and that's part of the strength of the team.
"Kimi put it behind him and did a great job in the race. George did an incredible job out front, and it'll be exciting to see them going at it in Malaysia."

detailZh: 迈凯伦车队据报将达成历史性的10亿美元收入里程碑
据报道，迈凯伦车队即将成为首支年收入突破10亿美元的F1车队
据天空新闻台报道，迈凯伦车队预计将成为首支年收入突破10亿美元的一级方程式车队。
报道称，迈凯伦赛车有限公司2025年度的账目将于本周提交。消息人士透露，这家位于沃金的车队将申报5.88亿英镑（约7.796亿美元）的收入。虽然该数字包含迈凯伦的印地赛车业务，但F1业务贡献了超过90%的总收入。
这些财务文件预计还将确认，迈凯伦赛车首席执行官扎克·布朗获得超过7540万英镑（1亿美元）的创纪录报酬，相比之下，2024年他的基本工资为600万英镑，另有3100万英镑的长期激励计划。
去年的这一数字与一笔因公司收购而触发的股票奖励有关。在此次收购中，巴林的穆姆塔拉卡特主权财富基金和阿布扎比的CYVN控股公司以35亿英镑的估值收购了迈凯伦赛车剩余30%的外部股份。
布朗在接受彭博社采访时谈到了2025年股权出售后一级方程式的增长。“这项运动现在火得一塌糊涂，你知道，每一个指标都是如此，对各车队的需求也是。不久之前，自由媒体集团才收购了这项运动，并设立了成本上限，这基本上确保了所有人的财务稳定、赛道上的稳定性和竞争力。
“所以这是一件非常好的事情。数以千万甚至上亿的观众前来观赛，赞助商和这项运动的合作伙伴数量也是前所未有的，所以这项运动正处于火热之中，希望它能一直持续下去。”
当被问及他是否认为一级方程式车队的估值已经达到顶峰时，布朗补充说："我不这么认为。我认为如果你看看整个体育界，我绝不自称是所有体育项目的专家，但体育的价值一直都在上涨。每次有创纪录的转播合同出现，无论是什么运动，大家都会说，'哦，那太疯狂了'。
"然后你回头看看，五年之后，价值仍在上涨。所以我认为我们的运动尤其还有很大的增长空间。我们有24场比赛，而市场需求大概能达到30场大奖赛，所以需求非常强劲。
"我们的赛车上拥有世界上最好的品牌，比如万事达卡、谷歌等等。竞争也非常精彩。去年有四支车队赢得了比赛，有七位不同的车手多次夺冠。
"这是我在关注这项运动的30年里第一次见到这样的情况，所以赛道上的竞争非常棒。而 Netflix 捕捉到的赛道之外的大戏也十分精彩。对大奖赛的需求从未如此强烈，所以我认为这项运动在许多方面才刚刚起步。"
detailEn: McLaren Racing reportedly set for historic $1billion revenue milestone
McLaren Racing is reportedly set to become the first F1 team to surpass $1billion in annual revenue
McLaren Racing is projected to become the first Formula 1 team to surpass $1billion in annual revenue, according to a report by Sky News.

The report states that McLaren Racing Ltd's accounts for the 2025 calendar year will be filed this week. Sources indicate the Woking outfit will declare revenue of £588million ($779.6million). While the figures include McLaren's IndyCar operations, F1 activities generated more than 90% of the total income.

The financial filings are also expected to confirm a record payout of over £75.4million ($100million) for McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown, compared with a £6million base salary and a £31million long-term incentive plan in 2024.

Last year's figure is tied to a share award triggered by the corporate buyout, in which Bahrain's Mumtalakat sovereign wealth fund and Abu Dhabi's CYVN Holdings acquired the remaining 30% of external shares in McLaren Racing at a valuation of £3.5billion.

Brown discussed the growth of F1 after the stake sale in 2025 during an interview with Bloomberg. "The sport is on fire, you know, every metric, demand for teams. It wasn't long ago that Liberty [Media] acquired the sport and put a cost cap in place, which kind of ensured everyone's financial stability and on-track stability and competitiveness.

"So it's been a wonderful thing. The fans are coming out in the tens and hundreds of millions, sponsors, partners in the sport, unlike we've ever seen before, so the sport is on fire, and long may it continue."

When asked if he felt valuations of F1 teams had reached their peak, Brown added: "I don't think so. I think if you look at sports in general, and I wouldn't say I'm an expert at all sports by any means, but they've only been going north forever. Every time there's a record deal and whatever sport it is, everyone goes, 'Oh, that was crazy'.

"And then you look back and in five years, they've still gone up. So I think our sport in particular has a lot of room for growth. We have 24 races, we have demand for probably 30 grands prix, so the demand is strong.
"Our car has the best brands in the world, the Mastercards, the Googles, etc. The competition is amazing. Last year, four teams won, seven different drivers won multiple races.

"It's the first time I've seen that in my 30 years of following the sport, so the on-track competition is great. The off-track drama, as captured by Netflix, is fantastic. The demand for grands prix has never been stronger, so I think the sport, in many ways, is just getting going."
